seo_title: What Does a Dermatologist Buy at Olive Young for Under $10?
dek: A 20-year dermatologist picks five Olive Young items with one verb each — erase, fill, cover, smooth, protect — and 1.75M viewers rebuild their routine around it.

takeaway.why_korea: Olive Young sale weeks are a national shopping event, and dermatologist-run channels have become the trusted filter over influencer hauls. This video is built as five verbs rather than five products, so viewers can slot it into a routine they already have, and the top comment is a viewer's own five-item recap with 547 likes — the comment section writes the shopping list for everyone else.
takeaway.best_for: Beginners assembling a first five-step routine; dry, sensitive or combination skin; anyone retinol-curious who wants the gentlest entry.
takeaway.skip_if: You want actives at prescription strength. Everything here is deliberately mild, and the retinol pick is a low-strength starter.

products.why: Step one, 'erase': the cleansing oil that both the doctor and the top comment start with.

products.name_en: Torriden Dive-In Low Molecular Hyaluronic Ampoule
products.why: Step two, 'fill': hydrating layer the comments assign to dry skin, with Wellage for oily skin.
Step three, 'cover': the barrier cream he recommends for dry and reactive skin.
Step four, 'smooth': a low-strength retinol built as an entry point, buffered with a cream.

products.name_en: Round Lab Birch Juice Moisturizing Sunscreen
products.why: Step five, 'protect': organic-filter daily sunscreen — and the one product commenters push back on hardest.

sentiment.method: editorial review of 80 top comments, weighted by likes
sentiment.note: Trust in the doctor is high and the purchase intent is visible. The scepticism is aimed at one product (the cleansing oil) and at copy-paste promo comments pedalling unrelated ampoules.

quote_specs.en: Wow, doctor — almost everything I use showed up here. I've tried a bit of everything and settled on Wellage and Torriden; I'd avoided ZEROID because of the price, but it's been the best of anything I've used. It's reassuring that everything you recommend is this gentle.
If the Ma:nyo cleansing oil doesn't suit you, your skin flips completely.
I bought the Ma:nyo oil because it's famous, but it's so oily and suffocating. Everyone has their own match, I guess.

Drop the birch one! It stings the eyes badly, it's irritating, and it doesn't block much — there are plenty of videos testing sunscreens side by side at the same dose, and the birch one comes near last.
quote_specs.note: A direct counterpoint to the video's final 'protect' step, from a commenter with 10 likes.

quote_specs.match: 저는 주름이랑 기미가 고민이라 올리브영 세일마다
quote_specs.en: I always wandered the Olive Young sale unsure what to buy for wrinkles and pigmentation, until a clinic manager told me about this ampoule — now it's the only thing I use.
quote_specs.label: Ad spam
quote_specs.note: Copy-paste promo comment from an account plugging an unrelated ampoule; several near-identical versions rank in the top 20. Real evidence of how ad spam colonises Korean comment sections.

caveat: Two cautions from the comment section itself: the Ma:nyo cleansing oil is the product most often named as a breakout trigger, and commenters argue the Round Lab birch sunscreen stings the eyes — patch test both before committing. The retinol is a starter strength; do not stack it with acids or prescription tretinoin.

body: Most routine videos fail because they assume you are starting from nothing. This one is organised around five verbs — erase, fill, cover, smooth, protect — which is why 1.75 million people watched a dermatologist walk through five Olive Young products in seventeen minutes. Each step is one product, all of them pharmacy-adjacent and mild, and the cheapest sits in the 10,000-won range.

The five are Ma:nyo's cleansing oil, a hyaluronic ampoule (Torriden for dry skin, Wellage for oily), ZEROID's barrier cream, a low-strength Theralogic retinol buffered with a moisturiser, and Round Lab's birch-juice sunscreen. What makes the video useful is the order: the retinol comes after the barrier cream, which is the sequencing most English-language retinol content skips.

The comment section does two jobs at once. The most-liked comment is a viewer's own recap of all five products with a note on which ampoule suits which skin type — effectively a free table of contents with 547 likes. And threaded among the genuine questions are two kinds of noise worth learning to spot: copy-paste promo comments pushing an unrelated ampoule, and a real disagreement about the sunscreen step, where commenters say the birch formula stings their eyes. Read the thread as a correction layer, not a fan club.
